transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith — I'll be talking with you today. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. But I know they've been watching my moves. They're changing the pallet counts on me, just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot.
Besides these concerns about being watched, have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people around you don't seem to notice?

Well, yeah, actually. I mean... sometimes when I'm down in the aisle at the warehouse, or even just at home folding clothes, I hear this man's voice. It's clear as day. He just tells me, Nicole, check it again. But whenever I look up, there's nobody anywhere near me.
How long have you been noticing these thoughts about being watched and hearing that man's voice—days, weeks, or months?
I'd say it's been going on for a while now. The voices and that feeling that people are watching me or changing the counts... it's been happening for about eight months.

During these past eight months, have you also gone through stretches of feeling extremely down, hopeless, or low on energy, or alternatively periods of feeling unusually elated, energetic, or needing very little sleep?

Well, yeah, there have been times like that. Not so much feeling down, but definitely the energetic part. There have been weeks where I'll sleep maybe three hours a night. I'll wake up way before my alarm even goes off, and I just feel totally fine. Like I don't even need any more rest to get moving and start my day.
During the times when you were not feeling that burst of energy or reduced need for sleep, did you still hear that man's voice or feel that people were watching and changing the counts?

Yeah, I did. There was a quieter few weeks, actually, where I was sleeping closer to normal and just... not racing around as much. But even then, I still heard the voice telling me to check things. And I still knew that people were changing the pallet counts against me.
Out of the full eight months since this all started, roughly how many weeks or months were you in one of those energetic, low-sleep-need periods, compared to the time you felt more your usual self?

I'd say it's been for more than half of this whole stretch. Most of the time, honestly, I've had those fired-up periods where I sleep very little and just take on way too much work. And I get pretty irritable when anyone tries to slow me down or tell me to take a break.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports 8 months of persistent psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions about coworkers/husband altering pallet counts to block her promotion, and auditory hallucinations of a man's voice commanding her to 'check it again'). Concurrently, for the majority of this period she describes a manic syndrome (decreased need for sleep to ~3 hours nightly with no fatigue, increased energy, overcommitment to tasks, irritability when slowed down). Critically, she confirms a distinct period of several weeks where the manic symptoms remitted (more normal sleep, less racing) yet the hallucinations and delusions persisted uninterrupted. This pattern—psychotic symptoms occurring both during and independent of a mood episode, with the mood episode present for the majority of the illness duration—meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features (which would require psychosis only during mood episodes) or schizophrenia (which would not account for the prominent, temporally-linked manic syndrome).
